Saudi Arabia has been exporting crude so far this month at a rate that suggests the kingdom has lifted its oil production toward the 9-10 million b/d range.

Using both the Persian Gulf and (more importantly) the Red Sea, Riyadh has boosted crude exports during the first 22 days of October to >7 million b/d, reaching pre-war levels (see @Vortexa chart below). Adding clean and dirty refined product, the export flow Oct 1-22 reaches ~8.5m b/d, slightly below pre-war levels of >9m b/d. 

The crude export surge -- and the production boost -- could be part of a "use-while-you-can" strategy aimed at pumping ahead of the potential restart of the war post US midterms (or before the Houthis of Yemen damage another key oil installation -- several near misses already in recent days, including an attack that killed two contractors near a major oilfield).

Note: using Oct 1-2 as typically it takes at least five days for dark transits across the SoH to become clear.

<Meeting of the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council with the Supreme Leader>
-Emphasis on Fulfilling Iran’s Conditions Aimed at Ending the War

Major General Dr. Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, met with the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei.

During this meeting, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei referred to the Supreme National Security Council and its secretariat as the "crossroads of prudence" in managing the country's affairs, emphasizing the mutual influence across the four domains of "culture," "politics," "economy," and "security," as well as the necessity of attaching appropriate policy frameworks to decision-making in each sector.

The Supreme Leader of the Islamic Revolution stated that having a roadmap based on a complete picture of every action—from inception to completion—is a prerequisite for making firm and well-founded decisions.

Strengthening national cohesion, unity, and mutual trust between the people and authorities; utilizing the constitutional capacity, especially Article 176, to assist the President and executive bodies in facilitating and expediting solutions to the nation’s problems; safeguarding national and regional security by exercising control over the Strait of Hormuz; and consolidating bilateral relations with neighboring countries grounded in sustainable, mutual interests were among the other key topics addressed in this meeting.

The Supreme Leader of the Islamic Revolution characterized the enemy’s desperation as a fruit of national resistance, underscoring active and timely public communication to sustain popular participation in defending the country and the system. He also emphasized pursuing the rights and interests of the Iranian nation and the Axis of Resistance through the realization of the conditions set forth by state officials to end the war and conclude the state of "neither war nor peace."

During this meeting, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council presented a report on the nation's conditions across various domains and current ongoing initiatives. In his report, Dr. Mohsen Rezaee highlighted the pursuit of the Islamic Republic's strategic policy toward "organizing endogenous regional arrangements and order" as one of the active measures undertaken by the secretariat of the Supreme National Security Council.

Silver continues to trade on a softer footing, hovering near an 11-month low, while gold’s ability to hold around USD 4,000 has pushed the gold-silver (XAUXAG) ratio higher towards 74.50. A sustained break above the 50% Fibonacci retracement at 74.66 could signal further relative weakness in silver, potentially opening the door to 82.30, the 61.8% retracement of the 2025–26 decline.

In a more pronounced downside scenario, a continued rise in the ratio towards the high 90s would imply silver trading in the low USD 40s, assuming gold remains near USD 4,000. While such an outcome is not our base case, silver has clearly lost some of its earlier momentum, with concerns about economic growth and fading speculative appetite weighing on sentiment. Silver’s tendency to amplify gold’s moves has also become a headwind as momentum-driven buying subsides.

As with gold, much of the recent selling appears to have been driven by momentum-focused hedge funds, reflected in a decline in the managed money net long to a 32-month low of just 3,746 contracts. In contrast, ETF demand has remained relatively resilient, with holdings rising to 25.1k tonnes, a seven-month high, from a July low of 24.3k tonnes. This divergence suggests that while speculative positioning has weakened considerably, longer-term investor interest remains intact.

For now, the key technical level to watch is 74.66 on the ratio, with a sustained break potentially pointing to further silver underperformance. Conversely, a rejection at this level could provide some near-term relief, with initial support around 72. Ultimately, gold remains the main source of directional guidance, while a sustained recovery in silver will likely depend on renewed momentum across the broader precious metals complex.
